housing_pipeline.description: The project proposes demolition of an existing two-story single-family dwelling and new construction of a new four-story two-unit residential building. New building to be entirely within required setbacks. Ministerial project pursuant to SB 423.

The proposed project is to construct a 9-story, 124-unit affordable, large family, housing building. At least 25% of the units will be 2-BR and 3BR each. At least 30% of the units will be 30%-AMI and permanently supportive. The remaining units, excluding the manager's unit, will be 50% AMI. The site is steeply sloped at approximately 10% along Pennsylvania Avenue. The main residential entry is at the first story near the street intersection. Residential services and amenities, including community room, property, manager and social services offices, bike parking, building utilities and storage are located on the first story. The second story includes residential units as well as the laundry room, ancillary community room, and an exit from the stories above. The third story includes residential units, a family day care unit, and the electrical room. The fourth through ninth story are similar and primarily contain residential units. The roof contains building utilities within an enclosed mechanical penthouse or visual / acoustical enclosure, a vegetated roof to mitigate stormwater, and photovoltaic panels. The roof will not be occupied except by for maintenance. Open space is located in a courtyard facing Pennsylvania Avenue on the on grade on the first story and over structure on the second story. Additional open space for stormwater treatment and for the family day care is located at level 3 at the south end of the site.

The site is currently vacant with no existing uses or structures. The site is partially excavated and retained and contains existing retaining walls, shoring, slabs on grade, and perimeter fencing.

The project site comprises six vacant parcels along San Bruno Avenue, with a frontage of 537.42' and an area of 25,182 sq. ft. The site has a large billboard and easements that allow for four buildable sites. The proposal is to utilize the State Density Bonus to construct 47 units in three separate buildings. Each will be three stories tall and two will include vehicle parking. Large open space and landscaping will be provided for the residents.

Modification to a previously approved project.

The project was approved under SB 330 and SB 35 and State Density Bonus law for 450 group housing units with 185 units of affordable housing with 41 units earning up to 55% AMI, 129 units earning up to 80% AMI and 15 units earning up to 110% AMI. The project now seeks to modify the existing approval to reduce the total unit count to 425 units with 100% of the units restricted as affordable as follows:  45 units at 30% AMI, 45 units at 50% AMI, 252 units at 60% AMI, 45 units at 70% AMI and 63 units at 80% AMI or less.   This modification results in a 5.6% decrease in unit count 

The project also seeks to modify the total square footage by reducing the development from 12 story building to an 11 story building, resulting in a reduction in GFA of 8.3%

MOHCD AMI levels as of 4 Feb 2026: 58 @ 40%; 150 @ 80%; 217 @ 100%

CONSTRUCTION OF A NEW 7-STORY MULTI-FAMILY RESIDENTIAL BUILDING WITH 92 DWELLING UNITS AT EXITING VACANT LOT in lieu of previously approved 57-unit 4-story project approved by Planning Commission Motion No. 19770. 

REQUEST A 50% STATE DENSITY BONUS per Planning Code Section 206.6 with waivers for height, rear yard, unit exposure, and horizontal mass reduction; and concession for ground floor floor-to-floor height.  In compliance with Sections 415 and 206.6, 15% of the 63 base project units would be affordable at 50% of AMI (9 units), 4.5% would be affordable at 80% of AMI (3 units) and 4.5% would be affordable at 110% of AMI (3 units), for a total of 15 BMR units and 77 market-rate units.

300 De Haro is a 12 story group housing project, situated at the corner of De Haro and 16th Streets. It will have 450 co-living units, ample and well designed indoor and outdoor common spaces, lively ground floor retail and amenity spaces, and parking for both bikes and cars. 

The project will use both SB-35 and the State Density Bonus to increase density and on-site affordabilty. Fifty three percent (53%) of the units will be affordable, for a total of 239 affordable units. Affordable units will be offered at various tiers: 40 units at 50-55% AMI, 185 at 80% AMI, and 14 at 110% AMI.

Conditional Use Authorization request for a change of use to develop an intermediate level of supportive housing. The proposed project will convert a licensing as an Residential Care Facility to an unlicensed group housing. No interior or exterior changes.

This proposal is a modification of the project that was approved by the Planning Commission on September 22, 2016 under Case No. 2013.0517ENX. The new project will utilize the State Density Bonus Program to construct a six-story, 70-foot-tall, 73,830-gross-square-foot residential building with 64 dwelling units.

The proposal is for a Conditional Use Authorization, pursuant to Planning Code Sections 303, 317, and 737 to demolish a mixed-use building containing one ground floor commercial space and one residential unit above, and to construct a five-story, 52-foot tall building containing one ground-floor commercial space and 12 residential units under the Individually Requested State Density Bonus Program pursuant to Planning Code Section 206.6 and California Government Code Section 65915. The project seeks a waiver from development standards for height, Planning Code Section 260, pursuant to State Density Bonus Law. The project also includes a lot merger of Block 5411, Lots 014 and 015.

Large Project Authorization request for a proposed seven-story mixed-use development consisting of 290 Group Housing units with associated common facilities and open space provisions. The subject property is triangular in shape, and has frontage on both 16th and De Haro Streets, with the hypotenuse of the triangle abutting a neighboring property. There is approximately 3,400 square feet of neighborhood serving commercial space located in two separate areas that activate the public realm. There are between 36 and 55 parking spaces primarily provided through a mechanical parking solution. Approximately 100 bicycle parking spaces are provided for building residents.

The property is an approximately 6.87-acre vacant parcel located on Jamestown Avenue north of Harney Way. The project proposes the construction of 122 dwelling units. The units will vary in size from 1,100 to 1,550 square feet, and each will contain two or three bedrooms. The project will contain 160,434 square feet of residential use in total. Most homes will be three-story attached townhome style condominiums with private garages at grade and approximately a quarter of them will be framed podium style condominiums. Two-thirds of the units will front shared paseos and have roof decks, while many of the remaining units will feature private patios and decks. The site will feature a network of shared open spaces.
